contraindications: Trying to make room for too many sensations at once may be overwhelming
original_extraction.evidence_text:
I said it before and I'll say it again: to practise expansion may be simple, but it sure isn’t easy. But
then again, what meaningful challenge is? Raising kids, keeping fit, nurturing a relationship,
developing a career, creating a work of art, caring for the environment: all these meaningful
challenges involve some difficulty. So why should practising expansion be any different? Like any
new skill, expansion is difficult to begin with, but as you continue to practise, it gets easier. Below
you'll find answers to common concerns and problems about expansion.

---

Q: I tried to make room for the feeling, but it was too overwhelming. What should I do?

---

A: You’re probably trying to do too much at once. Just pick one troublesome sensation and keep
your focus on it. Aim to accept just that one sensation, even if it takes you several minutes. Once
you’ve done that, go ahead and pick another one.

---

A: Yes, sometimes it is hard—at first. But like any skill, it gets easier with practice. Try to keep
your focus on one sensation at a time. If your attention wanders to another sensation, then as soon
as you realise it, bring your focus back to the first sensation.

---

A: Yes, this is the basic nature of the thinking self. It distracts you again and again, pulling you out
of your experience. So when it starts chattering, just say, ‘Thanks, Mind!’ or silently say to
yourself, ‘Thinking!’, then gently return your attention to the sensation. And whenever you notice
that your attention has wandered, take a second to note what distracted you (a memory, a thought,
an image); then gently refocus. Each time you do this, you are learning two valuable skills: first, to
notice when you’re all caught up in your thoughts (cognitive fusion); and second, to refocus your
attention after it has wandered.

---

Q: That was fantastic. The moment I made room for my unpleasant feelings, they disappeared. Is
this what I can expect every time?
generation_rules: Focus on one troublesome sensation at a time
Accept the sensation even if it takes several minutes
When attention wanders, note the distraction and gently refocus
pause_rules: Take a moment to note what distracted attention before gently returning focus to the sensation
original_extraction.psychological_function: Developing awareness of cognitive fusion, enhancing attentional control, reducing avoidance of unpleasant feelings, and increasing acceptance of internal experiences.
repetition_rules: Repeat the process of noticing distraction and refocusing attention each time it occurs
symbolic_elements: Saying 'Thanks, Mind!' or 'Thinking!' to acknowledge distracting thoughts
original_extraction.therapeutic_function: Practising expansion to accept and make room for unpleasant sensations, improving ability to focus on one sensation at a time, and learning to gently refocus attention when distracted by thoughts.
voice_rules: Use phrases like 'Thanks, Mind!' or 'Thinking!' to acknowledge thoughts without judgment
